sets.title: Stack extent and ABI alignment

objective_text.T58.01.a: Derive and defend: Prove result<=top-bytes, alignment and nonwrap; account for consumed padding and live stack bounds.
objective_text.T58.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement po_stack(top,bytes,out): require bytes<=top, subtract and round down to16-byte alignment; publish only on success. Treat integers as modeled addresses, not dereferenceable C pointers. Then build both assembly entry stubs with a private aligned stack and inspect the map.
objective_text.T58.01.c: Falsify and transfer: A port aligns to8 because pointers are8 bytes, violating the16-byte call boundary. A linker-defined top is not proof that subtraction stays in the reserved stack. Then Change to RV32E or Thumb and derive the appropriate ABI alignment from its specification rather than inheriting16. Add a guard region and test exact exhaustion.

sets.title: Argument register exhaustion

objective_text.T58.03.b: Implement and investigate: Implement po_arg(index,reg,offset) for the deliberately restricted nine-or-fewer uint64_t scalar interface: index0..7 maps to abstract argument registers0..7 with offset0; index8..15 maps to regUINT_MAX and stack offset8*(index-8); index>=16 rejects transactionally. sets.title: Owned context images

objective_text.T58.04.a: Derive and defend: Prove a save/restore preserves exactly the declared set and leaves nonowned registers untouched. State stack ownership, resume-address validity and exclusion of asynchronous FP/trap state.
objective_text.T58.04.b: Implement and investigate: Implement po_save(dst,arch,registers) copying only po_saved registers into a zero-filled32-slot image; reject arch>1 before mutation. po_restore validates image arch equals requested arch and copies only saved slots into a live register model, preserving others. Destination/source are disjoint. Extend assembly context switches using the same documented offsets.
objective_text.T58.04.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair restoration of an RV image as Arm by rejecting mismatched tags before any register mutation. A C struct size match does not establish semantic compatibility. Then Add two task stacks and a yield-return continuation; inject stack exhaustion and duplicate resume, and compare cooperative with asynchronous preemption save sets.

sets.title: Signed immediates and relocation ranges

objective_text.T58.05.a: Derive and defend: Derive sign-extension using unsigned extraction and subtraction in a range representable by int. Separate field representability, target instruction alignment and linker relaxation.
objective_text.T58.05.b: Implement and investigate: Implement po_sign12(raw) for the low12 bits as a mathematical signed value -2048..2047, ignoring higher bits. Implement po_branch(delta,bits,align) accepting only bits2..30, align2 or4 and aligned signed delta in [-2^(bits-1),2^(bits-1)-align]. Use this as a relocation admission oracle, not as a complete instruction encoder.
objective_text.T58.05.c: Falsify and transfer: Truncating an odd branch displacement silently redirects execution. A range-only check is insufficient; a passing assembler can still hide linker-added veneers. Then Encode RV B/J immediate bit scattering and compare with an independent assembler, then force an out-of-range AArch64 call and inspect its veneer clobbers.

sets.title: Trap status versus call state

objective_text.T58.06.a: Derive and defend: Draw status before entry, after entry and after return. Explain which processor state is automatic, which is software saved and why a call-return instruction cannot replace a trap return.
objective_text.T58.06.b: Implement and investigate: Implement po_trap(status,from_supervisor) and po_return(status): trap records spp, copies sie to spie and clears sie; return restores sie from spie, sets spie1 and clears spp. Inputs are boolean fields; invalid input rejects without mutation. Compare the explicit model to supervisor CSR traces in a dedicated RV guest.
objective_text.T58.06.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair stale prior-privilege state after return and a nested handler that overwrites the first saved PC. The model cannot establish interrupt controller acknowledgement behavior. Then Port the same logical event to an AArch64 exception level and identify every register/return difference from an inspected architecture manual before implementing.

sets.title: Privilege-aware memory access

objective_text.T58.07.a: Derive and defend: Derive each access decision before dereferencing and identify omitted page-walk obligations: validity, canonical address, superpage alignment, access/dirty updates, translation synchronization and fault cause.
objective_text.T58.07.b: Implement and investigate: Implement po_access(user_page,supervisor,sum,mxr,r,w,x,operation), with boolean flags and op0 read,1 write,2 execute. User execution rejects supervisor-only pages. Supervisor execution always rejects user pages; supervisor reads/writes user pages require sum. Read requires r or mxr&&x; write requires w; execute requires x. This models the inspected SUM/MXR obligations, not a complete page walk.
objective_text.T58.07.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair a supervisor execute path that assumes SUM permits executing user memory. A model allow decision never grants C pointer provenance or physical access. Then Implement a bounded three-level page-table walker with synthetic tables, then compare RV64 Sv39 and the selected Arm translation regime; inspect their full manuals and record unresolved differences.
